item.title: New Zealand Election Too Close to Call Four Days From Vote
item.description: New Zealand’s governing National Party has seen its lead narrow in a key opinion poll just four days from a general election.
item.dc:creator: Tracy Withers

item.title: Big Take: Legal Fights Loom Over US Midterms (Podcast)
item.description: It’s Election Day in the US and a deluge of midterms-related lawsuits have already been filed, even though polls haven’t closed yet. Bloomberg legal reporter Zoe Tillman and Josh Wingrove, who covers the White House, join host David Gura to make sense of the latest legal fights.
item.dc:creator: David Fox and Julia Press

item.title: Midterms 2026 What to Watch: Voter Turnout, Trump Inflation Record
item.description: Donald Trump’s not on the ballot, but polls show voters are focused on affordability concerns during his current term.
item.dc:creator: Hadriana Lowenkron and Kate Sullivan

item.title: Trump Faces Referendum as Voters Head to Polls in Midterm Elections 2026
item.description: America’s referendum on President Donald Trump’s second term is underway.
item.dc:creator: Ted Mann

item.title: Singaporean Plan to Import Clean Power Hits Indonesian Hurdle
item.description: Indonesia will prioritize domestic energy needs over exporting electricity, according to a government minister, complicating a plan for the country to supply renewable power to Singapore.
item.dc:creator: Benjamin Liu

item.title: Block on US Warnings to Election Workers Lifted by Court
item.description: A US appeals court halted a judge’s order that barred the Trump administration from demanding state and local officials set aside certain ballots or threatening criminal prosecutions before and after Tuesday’s midterm contests.
item.dc:creator: Zoe Tillman

item.title: US Midterms Test Trumpism as One Nation Surges in Australia
item.description: The US midterms will test President Trump's political power at home and offer clues about the staying power of Trump-style politics globally. In Australia, the far-right One Nation party is surging in popularity with policies that echo Trump's agenda, including opposition to immigration and climate-change skepticism. United States Studies Centre Economic Security Director Hayley Channer joins "Bloomberg: The Asia Trade" to discuss what the US vote could mean for Trumpism abroad and the outlook for US-Australia relations. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Democrats Lose Bid to Halt DOJ Effort Over ‘Non-Citizen’ Ballots
item.description: Democratic Party groups lost a bid to temporarily block the Trump administration from pressuring states to set aside mail-in ballots of people the US claims are likely non-citizens, a significant win for federal officials less than 24 hours before the midterm elections.
item.dc:creator: Erik Larson

item.title: Trump Talks Reflecting Pool in Midterm Closing Message
item.description: "Balance of Power" focuses on the intersection of politics and global business. On today's show, Maria Teresa Kumar, President and CEO of Voto Latino, says Latino voters in Texas’ Rio Grande Valley who moved toward President Trump over the economy and border security are now being pushed back toward Democrats by high costs, tariffs and immigration enforcement. Kumar says businesses in the region are being hurt by workers being picked up by Border Patrol and ICE and by uncertainty over tariff costs. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Bloomberg Businessweek Daily: Apple Growth Decelerates (Podcast)
item.description:
The people, companies and trends shaping the global economy. Watch Carol and Tim LIVE every day on YouTube: http://bit.ly/3vTiACF
Apple posted decelerating sales growth in its September quarter, with China revenue missing estimates, in its first earnings report since John Ternus took over as CEO. The growth marks a slowdown from a 16% increase in the June quarter. Elswhere, Anthropic disclosed a twelve-fold increase in quarterly revenue while also revealing it intends to spend over $895 billion in the coming years, and Marvell agreed to buy Lumentum in an historic $115 billion deal.
On today's episode: Anurag Rana, Bloomberg Intelligence Senior Tech Analyst Mark Gurman, Bloomberg News Managing Editor for Global Consumer Tech Seth Fiegerman, Bloomberg News AI Editor Ryan Gould, Bloomberg News Deals Reporter (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Kumar: Costs, ICE Are Pushing Latinos Toward Democrats
item.description: Maria Teresa Kumar, President and CEO of Voto Latino, says Latino voters in Texas’ Rio Grande Valley who moved toward President Trump over the economy and border security are now being pushed back toward Democrats by high costs, tariffs and immigration enforcement. Kumar says businesses in the region are being hurt by workers being picked up by Border Patrol and ICE and by uncertainty over tariff costs. Kumar says Latino voters in Florida are also rethinking their support after the administration rescinded protections for people with Temporary Protected Status. Kumar says Democrats cannot take Latino turnout for granted and need an affordability agenda as well as accountability over ICE detention and enforcement. She speaks with Joe Mathieu and Kailey Leinz on Bloomberg’s "Balance of Power." (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Democrats Could Flip Senate Seat in North Carolina
item.description: Bloomberg's Erik Wasson joins "Balance of Power" to discuss the election day races in North Carolina. Former Governor Roy Cooper, a Democrat is expected to defeat Michael Whatley in a Senate race. But other contests are expected to be closer. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Supreme Court Will Not Set Aside Some California Ballots
item.description: The US Supreme Court rejected the Trump administration’s bid to set aside thousand of ballots from California. The administration said the votes were from 20,000 "likely" noncitizens. The justices refused to get involved in the case. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Robinhood CFO on Retail IPO Demand, Agentic Trading
item.description: Robinhood is competing with other retail brokerages over access to Anthropic's mega-IPO and others as they come to market. CFO Shiv Verma says the company continues to see demand for IPO access, adding, "We're making sure the companies know retail is here." He also discusses the use of AI agents in trading accounts, saying customers continue asking for more agentic tools. Verma also says Robinhood is seeing an increase in non-sports related trades on its prediction market platform. Plus, Bloomberg News White House Correspondent Kate Sullivan joins to discuss President Trump's remarks from the Lincoln Memorial reflecting pool just one day before midterm elections. Then, Satya Thallam, Former Senior Counselor in the Trump White House joins to discuss data center opposition as a major issue in the election. Finally, Rep. Mike Lawler (R-NY) joins to discuss his campaign strategy as New Yorkers head to the polls Tuesday. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Michigan Midterms, Apple Earnings & the Tech Selloff
item.description: The Close brings you the latest news and analysis leading up to the final minutes and seconds before and after the closing bell on Wall Street. Today's guests are Edward Jones Head of Investment Strategy Mona Mahajan, Detroit Regional Chamber President & CEO Sandy Baruah, North Rosedale Park Civic Association Vice President Eric Henry, Sperling Economic Strategies President Gene Sperling, Detroit Future City CEO Anika Goss, Morgan Stanley Investment Management Senior Portfolio Manager Andrew Slimmon, M12 Managing Partner Cheryl Cheng, Asymco Founder & Managing Director Horace Dediu, Seaport Research Partners Senior Analyst Jay Goldberg, IDC Senior Director, Data & Analytics Nabila Popal, & Maxim Group Managing Director & Senior Consumer Internet Analyst Tom Forte. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Inspector General Hits Pulte Over ‘Unprecedented’ Obstruction
item.description: The nation’s top housing regulator took “unprecedented” steps to hinder investigations by its inspector general, the watchdog told lawmakers in a report published Monday.
item.dc:creator: Katy O'Donnell and Erin Schilling

item.title: Trump’s DOJ Rejected by Supreme Court on California Ballots
item.description: The US Supreme Court rejected the Trump administration’s bid to force thousands of California ballots to be set aside in the midterm election, dealing the president a high-profile setback as he presses his unproven claims of widespread illegal voting by noncitizens.
item.dc:creator: Greg Stohr

item.title: Iowa Becomes Real Test for Trump and GOP
item.description: President Donald Trump is looking to keep Iowa in Republican control. Senate candidate Ashley Hinson is in a tight race to hold on to retiring GOP Senator Joni Ernst's seat. There is also an open governor's race and several House battles that could determine control of Congress. Bloomberg's Skylar Woodhouse reports from Des Moines. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Trump Chooses DC Reflecting Pool For Midterm Elections Closing Argument
item.description: President Donald Trump used a speech on the eve of midterm elections that will shape his final two years in office to tout his months-long renovation of the Lincoln Memorial Reflecting Pool.
item.dc:creator: Jeff Mason

item.title: Khamenei Empowers Talks as Trump Says Iran Deal Could Happen
item.description: Iran President Masoud Pezeshkian said his government has been granted more authority by the country’s supreme leader to pursue peace talks, as President Donald Trump hinted at progress in negotiations.
item.dc:creator: Arsalan Shahla, Eltaf Najafizada and Jeff Mason
